failures.title: Peugeot EB2DT Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Wet Timing Belt Degradation (The "Belt in Oil" Issue)
items.whatHappens: The EB2DT uses a timing belt that runs inside the engine oil to reduce friction and noise. Over time, or if the incorrect engine oil specification is used, the belt material degrades and sheds rubber particles into the oil. These particles circulate and block the oil pickup strainer in the sump, leading to severe oil starvation. This often manifests first as a stiff brake pedal (due to vacuum pump starvation) before progressing to catastrophic engine bearing failure and seizure.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early via a drop in oil pressure or brake servo issues, the sump can be removed, the strainer cleaned, and the belt replaced. However, if the engine has already suffered oil starvation damage (indicated by bearing knock), a full reconditioned Peugeot EB2DT engine replacement is the only reliable fix.

items.title: Excessive Oil Consumption & Carbon Buildup
items.whatHappens: The piston ring design and PCV system on early PureTech engines can lead to high oil consumption. This not only requires frequent top-ups but also accelerates the degradation of the wet timing belt and leads to heavy carbon buildup on the intake valves and turbocharger, reducing performance and efficiency.
items.repairVsReplace: Requires strict oil level monitoring and shortened service intervals (every 6,000-8,000 miles). If the engine has suffered bore scoring or turbo failure from oil starvation, a replacement is necessary.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2016 engines received minor revisions to the belt material specification and updated ECU oil-level monitoring, making them slightly less prone to rapid belt degradation. However, the fundamental "belt in oil" architecture remains a point of vigilance across all production years, and strict adherence to PSA-approved low-SAPS engine oil is non-negotiable .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the EB2DT
variants.intro: As a Specific page type with no distinct sub-codes listed in the inventory, this section focuses on accurate identification and avoiding common, costly misidentifications. The EB2DT engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the cylinder block and is also recorded on your vehicle's V5C registration document under "Engine Number". Owners and breakers frequently confuse the EB2DT with its higher-output siblings, the EB2ADT (110hp) and the EB2ADTS (130hp), or the naturally aspirated EB2FA (82hp). While all four share the same 1.2-litre 3-cylinder PureTech block architecture, the EB2DT features a specific turbocharger, intercooler, and ECU calibration for its 100hp entry-level output. The EB2FA lacks a turbocharger entirely, while the EB2ADT and EB2ADTS feature progressively larger turbos and different injection mappings. Fitting an EB2FA, EB2ADT, or EB2ADTS wiring harness, ECU, or ancillary components to an EB2DT host will result in incorrect fueling, persistent fault codes, and a non-running vehicle.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement EB2DT - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Peugeot EB2DT engine for sale can be a viable, budget-friendly option for older 208 projects, but it carries a severe inherent risk. Unless the seller can provide documented proof that the wet timing belt has been replaced recently with the correct PSA-approved part, and the oil pickup strainer has been inspected, you are highly likely to be inheriting a ticking time bomb of belt degradation. Learn more about used engines.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: For most owners, a reconditioned Peugeot EB2DT is the only sensible choice. A proper recon will proactively address the engine's known weaknesses by fitting a brand-new timing belt kit, replacing the tensioners, and ensuring the oil pickup strainer is completely free of debris, delivering peace of mind for the future. Explore reconditioned engine options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for low-mileage 308 projects where the engine is being stripped to the bare block. This allows for new piston rings to address oil consumption, comprehensive decarbonisation, and verification of the turbocharger, ensuring the engine matches the pristine condition of the host chassis. View rebuilt engine services.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting your replacement through our vetted network ensures the work is completed by specialists familiar with PSA PureTech systems and wet-belt procedures, backed by a nationwide warranty. Check supply and fit availability.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Peugeot 208 and 308 models (2012-2018) typically hold values between £2,000 and £8,000, depending heavily on age, mileage, and body condition . Because a fully fitted, reconditioned Peugeot EB2DT engine replacement can approach £2,850, it is crucial to evaluate the vehicle's overall condition before committing to a major mechanical investment. Older 208 models valued under £3,500 frequently sit at the scrap threshold. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value first.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the Peugeot EB2DT engine?
items.answer: The most critical failure on the EB2DT is wet timing belt degradation, where the belt material breaks down and sheds rubber particles into the engine oil. These particles block the oil pickup strainer, leading to severe oil starvation and catastrophic engine bearing failure. A stiff brake pedal (due to vacuum pump starvation) or a cold-start rattle are primary early warning signs. If the engine has suffered oil starvation damage, a full reconditioned replacement is the only reliable fix.

items.question: Which Peugeot models use the EB2DT engine?
items.answer: The EB2DT 1.2-litre PureTech turbo petrol engine was fitted to the Peugeot 208 and 308 between 2012 and 2018. It served as the entry-level 100hp petrol option across Peugeot's core hatchback lineup. It was designed to replace the older 1.6-litre VTi and THP engines with improved fuel economy and lower emissions.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned EB2DT engine?
items.answer: For any Peugeot 208 or 308, a reconditioned EB2DT is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the high risk of wet-belt failure. Used engines almost always inherit the same degraded timing belt or blocked oil pickup strainer that caused the original removal. A proper reconditioned build proactively installs a brand-new PSA-approved timing belt kit, replaces the tensioners, and ensures the oil pickup strainer is completely clear. Reconditioned units also include comprehensive compression and oil pressure testing to guarantee reliability.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the EB2DT engine?
items.answer: You can confirm your engine code by checking the V5C registration document under the "Engine Number" field or by locating the code stamped on the cylinder block. The EB2DT is easily distinguished from the higher-output EB2ADTS (110hp/130hp) by its specific turbocharger and ECU calibration. It is also distinct from the naturally aspirated EB2FA (82hp), which lacks a turbocharger entirely. Fitting an EB2ADTS or EB2FA wiring harness or ECU to an EB2DT host will result in incorrect fueling and a non-running vehicle.
